summary: This note surveys folkloric creatures and cryptids across cultures, grouped by sky and sea monsters, forest dwellers, ghosts, guardians, elemental spirits, tricksters, and digital and screen media. It pairs each category with recent books, artworks and exhibitions from 2023-2024. It argues that folklore remains a living, evolving tradition that continues to inspire art and wonder.
one_line: A survey of folkloric creatures and cryptids worldwide, linking myths like the Kraken, Bigfoot and Kelpie to recent 2023-2024 books, art and media.
key_facts: Dr. Helena Watts published the essay collection "Hydra and Harpies: Sky and Sea Monsters in Global Mythology" on September 15, 2023.
The thunderbird is believed by certain North American Indigenous tribes to create thunder and lightning; artist Jacob Running Elk has depicted it in his work.
Stories of the Kraken, a gigantic sea monster said to dwell off the coasts of Norway and Greenland, have been told since the twelfth century.
Dr. Sebastian Clarke's book "Silent Sentinels: Tales of Cryptic Forest Dwellers from Around the World" began circulating in libraries as of October 7, 2023.
Artist Edie Morris painted Bigfoot (Sasquatch) in a series of mist-soaked paintings.
Kaito Nakamura's collection "Yurei: Elegy of the East" was displayed at Tokyo's Chiyoda Art Gallery in mid-November 2023.

The Scottish Kelpie is a shape-shifting water spirit that draws humans into the water but is also said to be a guardian against darker forces; sculptor Fiona McLeod has installations dating from December 2023.
In China, the lion-like Nian was believed to prey on villagers until scared away by the color red and loud noises; Nian art adorns streets and homes at Lunar New Year.
Paracelsus, a Swiss Renaissance physician and alchemist, categorized elemental spirits into undines (water), sylphs (air), gnomes (earth), and salamanders (fire).
Emily Torres launched the graphic novel series "Whispers of the Elements" on January 10, 2024.
Dr. Lisa Moreno curated a 2024 exhibition titled "Shape-Shifters: The Trickster in World Mythology".
Marcus Li, a digital folklorist, began compiling an online "Cryptozoological Map of the World" in late 2023, featuring art by digital artists such as Lara Chen.
The television series "The Mist of Avalon" introduced new generations to folkloric creatures, while independent filmmakers used crowdfunding to bring lesser-known cryptids to film.
